question: A 72-year-old man comes to the physician because of several episodes of dark urine over the past 2 months. He has had a 6 kg (13.2-lb) weight loss over the past 3 months despite no changes in appetite. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. A CT scan shows a heterogeneous enhancing mass arising from the left renal pelvis. Pathologic examination of the lesion is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Ulcerating tumor comprised of glandular cells within mucinous material
options.opb: Pedunculated tumor comprised of pleomorphic urothelial cells with severe nuclear atypia
options.opc: Tumor with central scar comprised of large eosinophilic cells with central nuclei
options.opd: Bright yellow tumor comprised of polygonal cells filled with lipids and glycogen
options.ope: Grayish-tan tumor comprised of primitive blastemal cells forming abortive glomeruli

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "72-year-old man with dark urine" -> "possible renal pathology" -> "CT scan shows heterogeneous mass" -> "mass arises from left renal pelvis" -> "likely renal cell carcinoma" -> "pathologic examination shows atypical cells" -> "possible pleomorphic urothelial cells" -> "severe nuclear atypia" -> 85%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with weight loss and smoking history" -> "risk factors for renal cancer" -> "CT scan reveals mass in renal pelvis" -> "pathologic findings expected in renal tumors" -> "possible presence of glandular cells" -> "mucinous material may be present" -> "less likely than urothelial carcinoma" -> 70%

CHAIN: "CT scan shows mass in renal pelvis" -> "consider differential diagnoses" -> "possible transitional cell carcinoma" -> "characteristic findings include pleomorphic cells" -> "nuclear atypia is common" -> "supports diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Heterogeneous mass in renal pelvis" -> "pathologic examination needed" -> "possible findings include lipid-filled cells" -> "less common in renal pelvis tumors" -> "more typical of renal oncocytoma" -> "not the most likely finding" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Mass in renal pelvis with atypical features" -> "consider embryonal tumors" -> "primitive blastemal cells forming glomeruli" -> "more typical of Wilms tumor" -> "unlikely in a 72-year-old man" -> "not consistent with age or presentation" -> 50%
analysis: The clinical presentation of dark urine, weight loss, and a CT scan showing a heterogeneous mass in the renal pelvis suggests a renal cell carcinoma, likely transitional cell carcinoma given the location. The most characteristic finding in such tumors is the presence of pleomorphic urothelial cells with severe nuclear atypia, which aligns with option 'opb'.
